question: Your support agent's system prompt tells it to use process_refund whenever a customer mentions a refund. The lookup_order description clearly states that it returns order and refund status, and its example queries include checking whether a refund has been paid. Logs show that refund status questions, such as whether the refund for order 4471 has gone through, trigger process_refund calls instead of lookup_order calls. What is the most likely cause of this misrouting?

options.text: The lookup_order description lacks input formats and example queries, so the model cannot tell that refund status questions belong to lookup_order instead of process_refund.
options.reason: The scenario says the lookup_order description already covers refund status and gives matching example queries, so a weak description is not the cause.

options.text: The tool_choice setting is "auto", which lets the model ignore tool descriptions, so the agent picks process_refund at random for refund messages.
options.reason: With "auto" the model still selects tools from their descriptions, so this setting does not explain why refund status questions consistently go to process_refund.

options.text: The process_refund tool returns failures without the isError flag, so the agent keeps calling it instead of switching to lookup_order for status questions.
options.reason: Error reporting affects recovery after a call, but the logs show the wrong tool is chosen in the first place, which points to the system prompt wording.

options.text: The keyword-sensitive refund instruction in the system prompt ties the word refund to process_refund and overrides the clear lookup_order description.
options.reason: The guide states that keyword-sensitive system prompt wording can create unintended tool associations that override well-written tool descriptions.
